basis: Spastic ataxia, epilepsy and sensorimotor neuropathy define the disease; weakness and amyotrophy are neuropathic, and oculomotor apraxia is neurologic.
B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia is a blood and marrow neoplasm; no common additional organ damage is established.
Hypogonadism and cataracts define the syndrome; osteoporosis occurs in 80-99% and fractures in 30-79%.
Severe developmental and intellectual disability define the disorder; short distal phalanges in 4/9 are minor dysmorphism without established skeletal dysfunction.
Primary thyroid carcinoma; airway obstruction, laryngotracheal stenosis and lung tumor involvement are frequent (30-79%), supporting direct pulmonary involvement.
Renal tubular aldosterone resistance causes salt wasting, hyperkalemia and metabolic acidosis; urinary infection is an underlying trigger rather than this disorder itself.
High-grade glioma arising in the childhood central nervous system.
Developmental disability and sparse hair define it; kidney abnormalities 30-79%, VSD 3/8. Common skeletal abnormalities omitted under the four-axis cap.
Neurodevelopmental impairment defines the syndrome; nonspecific palate and pinna morphology do not establish functional organ damage; heart anomalies occur in under 30%.
Inherited platelet dysfunction and impaired coagulation define this bleeding disorder.
Hereditary prostate cancer arises in a reproductive organ outside the defined axes; no qualifying additional organ involvement is established.
Progressive nephropathy and hypertension are defining features; renal failure, proteinuria and hematuria support kidney disease.
Defined by delusional misidentification, usually in psychosis; neurologic injury explains only a subset and is not intrinsic to the umbrella concept.
Inherited ataxia caused by PEX16 deficiency, a peroxisome biogenesis disorder; no evidence establishes common damage to additional organs in this ataxic form.
Inherited retinal degeneration with visual loss; retinal vessel attenuation and cataracts remain within the ocular axis.
Most transitional cell neoplasms arise in urinary urothelium; the umbrella also includes ovarian Brenner tumors, whose origin has no axis.
Lipid metabolic myopathy directly affects skeletal muscle; respiratory weakness is muscular, while cardiomyopathy and arrhythmia occur in under 30%.
TK2 metabolic deficiency causes myopathy; encephalopathy and seizures are annotated at 30-79%. Respiratory failure reflects muscle weakness rather than intrinsic lung damage.
Congenital myopathy; ophthalmoplegia and ptosis each 3/3, cleft palate 2/2. Reduced ventilation is attributable to muscle weakness; isolated developmental delay is insufficient.
Sterol synthesis disorder with defining skeletal and skin disease; cataracts in 6/8. Tracheal cartilage anomalies (30-79%) omitted under the four-axis cap.
Primary microcephaly with severe intellectual disability, developmental delay, cerebellar hypoplasia and seizures.
Growth disorder with reduced growth hormone annotated at 30-79%; global developmental delay also 30-79%. Feeding difficulty alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Glial tumor arising in the brain or spinal cord; no additional organ involvement applies to most patients across the group.
Type II collagen skeletal disorder with defining early generalized osteoarthritis and vertebral dysplasia; no common extra-skeletal damage is documented.
Cleft palate, ankyloglossia and associated dental abnormalities affect the oral cavity; digital abnormalities are not established as common damaging manifestations.
